title: Modi Invokes Pokhran at Somnath: India Will Not Bow
excerpt: On National Technology Day, PM Modi marks 28 years of Operation Shakti and praises Vajpayee's defiance of global sanctions.
body:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi marked the 28th anniversary of India's 1998 Pokhran nuclear tests on May 11 with a dual tribute — at Gujarat's Somnath Temple and on social media — calling Operation Shakti proof of the nation's unbreakable political will.

**What Modi Said at Somnath:**
Addressing the Somnath Amrit Mahotsav gathering, Modi invoked former PM Atal Bihari Vajpayee's resolve under fire. He said: 'On May 11th, the first three nuclear tests were conducted. Our scientists showcased India's capabilities to the entire world. Various sanctions were imposed...But on May 13th, two more nuclear tests were conducted. That demonstrated to the world just how unwavering India's political will truly is.' He credited the Vajpayee-led government for withstanding massive international pressure and placing the nation above all else. Modi also connected Operation Shakti's name to India's ancient Shiva-Shakti tradition, framing scientific achievement as an extension of civilisational identity.

**Why This Moment Carries Weight:**
Operation Shakti established India as the sixth country to join the nuclear club and reshaped South Asian security equations. Modi's remarks carry a broader strategic message — that India's rise as a global power rests on self-confidence and the readiness to absorb short-term costs for long-term sovereignty. On X, he separately saluted India's scientists on National Technology Day, calling the tests 'a landmark moment' that reflected India's *unwavering commitment* to self-reliance.

**What to Watch:**
With India-Pakistan tensions at a sustained high in 2026, watch for whether Modi's Pokhran invocations translate into fresh signals on nuclear doctrine or defence-technology investment in the coming weeks.
nri_angle: For Indian-Americans who lived through the sanctions era of 1998 and felt the sting of that moment, Modi's Pokhran tribute is a direct reminder of how far India's global standing has travelled — and why its strategic autonomy matters for the diaspora's identity and influence in Washington.
